questions.q: With a file selected, **Alt+Enter** shows —
options: The file in a new window
questions.solution: **Alt+Enter** opens Properties (size, dates, attributes) — the keyboard way of right-clicking and choosing Properties.

questions.q: How many **different values** can **8 bits** represent?
questions.solution: 2⁸ = **256** values, from 0 up to 255. 'Largest value' would be 255; 'number of values' is 256.

questions.q: The default file extension of a PowerPoint 2007 or later presentation is —
questions.solution: **.pptx** is the Office Open XML default (X = XML). .ppt is 97-2003, .ppsx is a show, .potx is a template.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU performs subtraction and comparison operations?
questions.solution: Arithmetic (add, subtract) and logical (compare, AND/OR) operations are executed in the ALU. The program counter is a register holding the next instruction's address; the CU only coordinates.
questions.shortcut: Any verb like add/subtract/compare/AND-OR -> ALU, no matter how the question dresses it up.

questions.q: Select the correct question tag.  Open the window, ___
questions.solution: An imperative takes **will you?** as its tag.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The doctor advised him not to eat fried food.
options: The doctor said to him, "Do not to eat fried food."
The doctor advised him, "Not to eat fried food."
The doctor said to him, "Do not eat fried food."
The doctor said to him, "You are not eating fried food."
questions.solution: The advice frame advised + not to + V1 reverses to the negative imperative: **said to him, 'Do not eat fried food.'** — the not goes back inside the quote as do not. 'Do not to eat' carries the frame's not into the quote wrongly; 'advised him, ...' keeps the reported verb with direct words; the eating version changes the sentence.
questions.shortcut: not to + V1 → 'Do not + V1' in the quote.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To break the ice
options: to start a conversation among people who feel shy or stiff
to melt ice for drinking water
questions.solution: *Break the ice* = to get people talking and relaxed in a new or awkward group. 'Melt ice' is the literal decoy; the other two have nothing to do with the picture.
questions.shortcut: Ice = stiffness between strangers; breaking it = starting talk.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: The tank 'taught them what the (4) ___ never did — that water is counted'. Only a **syllabus** is a thing that teaches in a school. The tempting *plumber* fits a water story locally, but re-reading shows the sentence is about a *lesson*, not a repair job — the plumber never set out to teach anything. The full-passage re-read catches this.
questions.shortcut: Two options may fit locally; re-read the passage and keep the one that does not clash with the sentence's real point (teaching).
questions.passage: Sunshine Public School used to buy tankers of water every summer. Last year it built a simple rainwater system: rain falling on the roof travels through pipes into a (1) ______ tank, where leaves and dust settle at the bottom. The cleaned water then runs into the school's old well, which had almost dried up. This summer the school did not order a single (2) ______, and the garden gate, once kept locked to protect the wilting plants, now stands open. The headmaster says the biggest change is in the students: they check the taps after (3) ______ and repair dripping ones the same day. 'The tank taught them what the (4) ______ never did — that water is counted, not limitless,' he says.

questions.q: Teflon, used in non-stick cookware, is a polymer of:
questions.solution: **Teflon** is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), made from **tetrafluoroethylene**. Vinyl chloride gives PVC, isoprene gives natural rubber and ethene gives polythene.

questions.q: **Rakhigarhi**, the largest Harappan site in India, lies in which state?
questions.solution: **Rakhigarhi** is in Hisar district, **Haryana**, on the Ghaggar plain. India's other key Harappan states are Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, UP and Maharashtra.
questions.shortcut: Two big Haryana sites: Rakhigarhi and Banawali.

questions.q: Kanishka ruled from **Purushpura**; his second capital in India was —
questions.solution: Kanishka's capitals were **Purushpura (Peshawar)** and **Mathura**. The Mathura art school also flourished under the Kushanas.

questions.q: Hiuen Tsang's travel record of India is titled —
questions.solution: **Si-yu-ki** ('Records of the Western World') is Hiuen Tsang's account; *Indica* was Megasthenes' book and the *Periplus* a Greek trade guide.

questions.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point $30\sqrt{3}$ m from its base is $30^\circ$. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution: $d = \sqrt3 h \Rightarrow h = \frac{30\sqrt3}{\sqrt3} = 30$ m.

questions.q: The population of a village is 6,400 and it increases at 25% per annum. Its population after 2 years will be:
A and B invest ₹6,000 and ₹4,000 in a business. B manages the business and receives 10% of the profit as salary. If the annual profit is ₹9,000, what does A receive?
questions.solution:
B's management salary = 10% of 9,000 = ₹900. Residue = ₹8,100.
Capital ratio = 6,000 : 4,000 = 3 : 2.
A gets $\frac{3}{5} \times 8100$ = ₹4,860 (B gets ₹3,240 + ₹900 = ₹4,140).
questions.shortcut: Cut 10% off the top, split 3 : 2: A = 3/5 × 8,100 = ₹4,860.

questions.q: In a class of 50 students, 30 play cricket and 25 play football. If 5 students play neither game, how many students play both?
questions.solution:
Playing at least one: $50 - 5 = 45$.
Both $= 30 + 25 - 45 = 10$.

questions.q:
Select the term that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**B2, D4, F8, H16, ?**
questions.solution: Letters B, D, F, H (+2) → J. Numbers 2, 4, 8, 16 (×2) → 32. Answer **J32**.

questions.q: If **× means ÷**, **÷ means +**, **+ means −** and **− means ×**, then what is the value of **[(60 × 4) + 5] − 2 ÷ 7**?
questions.solution: Rewrite: **[(60 ÷ 4) − 5] × 2 + 7**. Inner bracket: 60 ÷ 4 = 15. Square bracket: 15 − 5 = 10. Then 10 × 2 + 7 = 20 + 7 = **27**. (10 × (2 + 7) = 90 is the trap of adding before multiplying.)
questions.shortcut: Solve the brackets fully, then × before +.

questions.q:
Three of the following four pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd pair.

**Carpenter : Saw, Tailor : Needle, Farmer : Plough, Doctor : Hospital**
questions.solution: Carpenter - saw, tailor - needle and farmer - plough are **worker : tool**. A hospital is the doctor's **workplace**, not a tool → **Doctor : Hospital**.

questions.q: Five friends **R, S, T, U and V sit in a row facing south. R sits in the exact middle. T sits second to the left of R. V sits immediately to the right of R. S sits at an extreme end.** Who sits **immediately to the left of R** (from R's own facing)?
questions.solution: Facing south, R's left is the viewer's right. R (seat 3) → T is second to R's left = seat 5; V immediately to R's right = seat 2; S takes seat 1, leaving **U at seat 4 — immediately to R's left** (viewer's right of R).
questions.shortcut: South-facing row: swap 'left' and 'right' for the people, keep the end seats as drawn.
